Hi Sébastien — thanks for the thoughtful questions and for taking the time. I pulled together a short Q&A and attached a one-page FAQ that addresses the points below; I also looped in Marcus (Product Security) and Stephanie (Legal) for any necessary technical or contractual detail.

Quick answers up front:
- Hosted API: you can choose EU-only hosted region (Frankfurt or Amsterdam) and we guarantee processing and tokenization occur in the chosen region.
- Subprocessors: primary infra is with GCP (europe-west1) for our EU regions; we also use S3-compatible object storage for long retention in eu-west-1 (AWS) for some accounts that opt in — full subprocessors list attached and in the DPA.
- Transfers: for transfers outside the EEA we rely on European Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) supplemented by contractual controls in our DPA. We do not rely solely on self-attestation.
- Retention/deletion: default logs (operational telemetry) retained 90 days; request/response payloads retained 30 days by default for hosted accounts unless customer requests shorter retention or enables automatic purging; customers can request deletion of specific data via a support ticket and we provide an audit trail for deletion events.

Attachments in this message: RBW-Residency-and-Subprocessors-FAQ.pdf (1 page) — short table of regions, active subprocessors, and transfer mechanisms.

Hi Sébastien — adding a few implementation notes from Product Security: 

- Region isolation: when you pick an EU-hosted instance we pin inference containers, tokenizers, and ephemeral KV caches to EU-only GPU pools. Persistent storage used for model artifacts and any customer-controlled cache is configured per-region.
- Subprocessors list (summary): GCP (primary compute), AWS (s3 object store for opt-in long-term archival), Fastly (CDN for static assets), Segment (optional telemetry ingestion for partners). We provide a full subprocessors spreadsheet in the DPA appendix.
- Cross-border: when a customer's account is configured for EU-only processing we ensure no automatic routing to US regions for staged capacity; we do offer a failover policy that stays within EU unless explicitly configured to allow a cross-region fallback (we recommend keeping fallback disabled for regulated workloads). Any outbound transfer to non-EEA regions is covered by SCCs and contract language; for customers requiring additional assurance we support executing a custom DPA and can add contractual constraints on subprocessors.
- Deletion flow: customer submits deletion request via support portal or API; request is triaged, a deletion job runs that purges payloads and KV caches, and we return a signed deletion confirmation. For accounts with Dedicated/Private deployments, deletion is handled directly on customer-managed storage.

I'll attach the subprocessors table and sample SCC clause to the legal thread.
